answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a stake-backed vouch registry: each identity locks collateral and is vouched by two already-staked peers, forming a trellis of cross-signed links rather than a headcount of keys. If a node is caught faking identity, the slash sends a ripple up the voucher chain, burning its sponsors' collateral too. The attacker pays twice per clone, so minting N Sybils costs N times the deposit and one detection wipes the branch. An open atlas of those links lets any auditor see who backed whom: cost grows linearly while one honest report can destroy the farm.
